name: Dian
text: Dian is an Irish name that means swift, rapid, intense, or strong. Several figures of early Irish narrative bore the name. Dian I stands as the son of the malevolent Carman. With his brothers he helped bring ruin upon Ireland. A second Dian served as a young Fianna chief under Fionn mac Cumhaill. This second Dian was carried off into the Otherworld by the sidh folk. On coming back he gave a single answer. He would rather serve the Fianna as a follower than sit as king across in the Otherworld. His remark matches what Achilles says to Odysseus in the Odyssey. The name Dian therefore marks both a destroyer of Ireland and a homesick Fianna hero. Each bearer of the name keeps the sense of swiftness.

okr.objective: Dian as an Irish name borne by Carman's son and by a Fianna chieftain taken to the Otherworld.
key_results: Dian means swift or strong in Irish.
Dian I was the son of Carman and joined in laying waste to Ireland.
A second Dian was a Fianna chieftain taken to the sidh.
On returning, the second Dian preferred Fianna service to Otherworld rule.
His remark echoes Achilles speaking to Odysseus.
